<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915661_theRebbe_783" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915661_theRebbe_783__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that gemilus chasadim for the wealthy involves an influence from chesed that is above the level of wealth itself.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And the maamar continues,</t>
    <t s="2">that it is stated in the Gemara37</t>
    <t s="3">that tzedakah is for the poor and gemilus chasadim is both for the poor and for the wealthy.</t>
    <t s="4">From this</t>
    <t s="5">(that gemilus chasadim is also for the wealthy)</t>
    <t s="6">it is understood,</t>
    <t s="7">that the influence from the aspect of chesed is above the level of a wealthy person.</t>
    <t s="8">And to note,</t>
    <t s="9">that ostensibly one could say that the influence of chesed to a wealthy person is that they are granted a greater wealth than the wealth they had previously.</t>
    <t s="10">And what is said in the maamar, that the influence from the aspect of chesed is above the level of a wealthy person,</t>
    <t s="11">one could say,</t>
    <t s="12">that when the influence that is now granted to him is a matter that is commensurate with his level,</t>
    <t s="13">then,</t>
    <t s="14">since previously he lacked the matter that is being granted to him</t>
    <t s="15">(even though the matter is commensurate with his level),</t>
    <t s="16">he is not</t>
    <t s="17">(the true essence of the matter of)</t>
    <t s="18">a wealthy person.</t>
    <t s="19">Therefore the maamar explains,</t>
    <t s="20">that gemilus chasadim for the wealthy is that the abundance from the aspect of chesed is above the level of a wealthy person,</t>
    <t s="21">meaning that it is of an entirely different category</t>
    <t s="22">(and that it has no matter that is not commensurate with his level at all,</t>
    <t s="23">is not a deficiency in his wealth).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the ultimate wealth of Shlomo's era came from the revelation of the inner aspect of Kesser, drawing down extraordinary wealth both physically and spiritually.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And in order to explain the matter of chesed that is above wealth,</t>
    <t s="2">the maamar precedes with an explanation of the matter of the wealth that existed in the days of Shlomo</t>
    <t s="3">(the most elevated level of wealth).</t>
    <t s="4">And it explains,</t>
    <t s="5">that this, that in the days of Shlomo the moon stood in its perfection38,</t>
    <t s="6">is,</t>
    <t s="7">that in addition to the five partzufim that were drawn into Malchus</t>
    <t s="8">(the moon,</t>
    <t s="9">Sihra)</t>
    <t s="10">which had been lacking,</t>
    <t s="11">there was also drawn into it the revelation of the innerness of Kesser,</t>
    <t s="12">Atik.</t>
    <t s="13">And from the wealth of Malchus</t>
    <t s="14">(Knesses Yisrael)</t>
    <t s="15">extraordinary wealth was drawn down to Yisrael even below,</t>
    <t s="16">extraordinary wealth in physicality, to the point that silver was not considered anything in the days of Shlomo39,</t>
    <t s="17">and extraordinary wealth in spirituality,</t>
    <t s="18">that specifically in the days of Shlomo the Beis HaMikdash was built,</t>
    <t s="19">for the revelation that was in the Beis HaMikdash is a more elevated revelation than the revelation that was in the Mishkan that preceded it.</t>
    <t s="20">And to add,</t>
    <t s="21">that this, that in the days of Shlomo there was a most elevated revelation,</t>
    <t s="22">was even before the Beis HaMikdash was built.</t>
    <t s="23">For that the building of the Beis HaMikdash was specifically by Shlomo</t>
    <t s="24">[even though the design of the Temple was made by Dovid40]</t>
    <t s="25">is as it is stated41</t>
    <t s="26">He</t>
    <t s="27">(Shlomo)</t>
    <t s="28">will be a man of rest etc. and peace and quiet I will give upon Yisrael in his days</t>
    <t s="29">(and therefore)</t>
    <t s="30">he will build a house for My Name etc.,</t>
    <t s="31">and it is known,</t>
    <t s="32">that this, that all the nations were nullified to Shlomo</t>
    <t s="33">[therefore in his days there was rest and peace]</t>
    <t s="34">was that they were nullified to the revelation of Ein Sof that shone through him42.</t>
    <t s="35">And likewise regarding this, that they came to him from all the nations to hear his wisdom43,</t>
    <t s="36">the true reason for this, that they came to him, is because they were drawn to G-dliness</t>
    <t s="37">(and in the manner of what is stated44</t>
    <t s="38">regarding Moshiach45</t>
    <t s="39">and all the nations will stream to him,</t>
    <t s="40">that this, that everyone will be drawn to him, is that they will be drawn to G-dliness).</t>
    <t s="41">For the revelation of light that shone then,</t>
    <t s="42">drew to itself the sparks that were among the nations,</t>
    <t s="43">similar to a torch that draws all sparks to itself46.</t>
    <t s="44">And since the revelation that shone then was a most elevated revelation,</t>
    <t s="45">therefore,</t>
    <t s="46">even the sparks in the distant places47</t>
    <t s="47">were drawn to the revelation that shone through Shlomo,</t>
    <t s="48">as it is stated48</t>
    <t s="49">And the Queen of Sheba heard the fame of Shlomo for the Name of G-d etc. and she came to Yerushalayim etc.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section contrasts the refinement through the Mishkan, which was through war, with the refinement through the Beis HaMikdash, which was through rest, and explains the true meaning of rest.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, that Shlomo was a man of rest,</t>
    <t s="2">that the refinement in his days was in a manner of rest</t>
    <t s="3">[that there was no need for war in order to refine the sparks,</t>
    <t s="4">rather the sparks were drawn to him on their own,</t>
    <t s="5">to be refined],</t>
    <t s="6">this was primarily through the revelation that shone in the Beis HaMikdash.</t>
    <t s="7">For the refinement through the revelation that shone in the Mishkan,</t>
    <t s="8">including also the revelation that shone in the Ark that was in the Mishkan,</t>
    <t s="9">was in a manner of war,</t>
    <t s="10">and the refinement through the revelation that shone in the Beis HaMikdash was in a manner of rest.</t>
    <t s="11">As it is stated in the Zohar49,</t>
    <t s="12">There were two who said "Arise, Hashem",</t>
    <t s="13">Moshe and Dovid,</t>
    <t s="14">Moshe said50</t>
    <t s="15">"Arise, Hashem, and let Your enemies be scattered",</t>
    <t s="16">and Dovid said51</t>
    <t s="17">"Arise, Hashem, to Your resting place."</t>
    <t s="18">And it is explained in the maamar52,</t>
    <t s="19">that this, that the Mishkan and the Ark traveled in the desert in order to nullify the klipos that were in the desert</t>
    <t s="20">(snakes, serpents, and scorpions)</t>
    <t s="21">and to refine and elevate the sparks of holiness that had fallen there,</t>
    <t s="22">is a refinement in a manner of war.</t>
    <t s="23">Like a king who goes out from his place and goes to the enemy's country to fight him and conquer him.</t>
    <t s="24">Therefore Moshe said</t>
    <t s="25">[regarding the journeying of the Ark in the desert—"And it was, when the Ark journeyed"]</t>
    <t s="26">"Arise, Hashem, and let Your enemies be scattered",</t>
    <t s="27">for there are enemies that one must fight against.</t>
    <t s="28">And the refinement through the revelation that shone in the Beis HaMikdash was in a manner of rest,</t>
    <t s="29">for Shlomo was in his place and the sparks were drawn to him on their own.</t>
    <t s="30">Therefore Dovid said "Arise, Hashem, to Your resting place."</t>
    <t s="31">And to note,</t>
    <t s="32">that in many places53</t>
    <t s="33">it is explained,</t>
    <t s="34">that the refinement that was through the journeying of the Ark in the desert is a refinement in a manner of rest.</t>
    <t s="35">For the matter of rest that is explained there is that the refinement is in a spontaneous manner.</t>
    <t s="36">And since the nullification of the klipos and the refinement of the sparks that fell into them through the revelation that shone in the Mishkan was in a spontaneous manner,</t>
    <t s="37">therefore,</t>
    <t s="38">even the refinement through the Ark of the Mishkan is called a refinement in a manner of rest.</t>
    <t s="39">But the true matter of rest is that the one who refines does not descend to the place of that which is being refined, but rather remains in his place,</t>
    <t s="40">and through the revelation of light</t>
    <t s="41">(of the one who refines)</t>
    <t s="42">that shines upon that which is being refined,</t>
    <t s="43">it is drawn on its own to the one who refines.</t>
    <t s="44">And rest in this manner was specifically in the days of Shlomo.</t>
    <t s="45">[And in the manner of what is known54</t>
    <t s="46">regarding the matter of refinement through Torah,</t>
    <t s="47">that in general,</t>
    <t s="48">even the refinement through the revealed aspect of Torah is in a manner of rest.</t>
    <t s="49">For since the refinement is in a spontaneous manner</t>
    <t s="50">(for by learning Torah, that this thing is permitted and this thing is forbidden,</t>
    <t s="51">they are refined spontaneously.</t>
    <t s="52">And not like the refinement of prayer, which is through the G-dly soul clothing itself in the animal soul),</t>
    <t s="53">therefore,</t>
    <t s="54">even the refinement through the revealed aspect of Torah is called a refinement in a manner of rest.</t>
    <t s="55">But in particular,</t>
    <t s="56">since the refinement through the revealed aspect of Torah is through it descending and clothing itself in physical matters,</t>
    <t s="57">this is a matter of war</t>
    <t s="58">[in the manner of the king going out from his place and going to the place of the enemy],</t>
    <t s="59">and the true matter of refinement in a manner of rest is in the refinement through the inner aspect of Torah].</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
